verdicts.note: Roblox's 7 Jan 2026 release (BusinessWire/Nasdaq republication) confirms: Persona facial age estimation or ID check (13+) required for chat; six bands under 9 / 9-12 / 13-15 / 16-17 / 18-20 / 21+; default chat only with the band directly above and below; chat off for under-9 without parental consent; December 2025 enforcement in Australia, New Zealand and the Netherlands. Nuance: January rollout began with US users and reached all other chat regions 'over the following week'; Roblox says bands may vary by region/product and that it will ask users to re-run the check when behaviour suggests a different age. Images are processed by Persona and deleted after estimation.

Confirmed: WV ~$11.1m, AL $12.2m, NV $12.5m, total $35.8m (Bloomberg 21 Apr 2026; Insurance Journal) — but Nevada was announced 15 Apr and AL/WV on 21 Apr, so '21 April' is only the AL/WV date. Kansas confirmed: $9.8m to the AG over three years plus a $500k awareness campaign, announced 29 Sep 2026 (KCTV5). Correction: South Dakota (13-14 Jul 2026) is reported as a $15m package over four years with $8.6m guaranteed to the state (SDPB/KOTA), not '~$10m'. Mississippi settlement confirmed by Roblox's Q2 2026 10-Q (settled states as of 30 Jul 2026: AL, MS, NV, SD, WV; 'negotiating with other states') but the June 2026 date and the Mississippi amount were not found. The pending-suit list (TX, FL, TN, IA, NE) was not searched. The brief's '~$54m' total depends on which SD figure is used and on the unverified MS amount; present it as a range.

8579 LLC £1.35m (s.12 breach, 25 Jul to at least 19 Nov 2025) plus £50k information-request penalty, with a 23 Feb 2026 compliance deadline and £1,000/day penalty, confirmed (Inforrm; The Record; Freevacy). Kick Online Entertainment £800k confirmed; the paired information-request penalty is reported as £30k + £200/day (Inforrm, Express & Star) but £50k + £250/day by Freevacy — check Ofcom's decision before quoting. AVS Group £1m + £50k and the 25 Jul 2025 / £18m-or-10% figures were not re-searched (budget) but are consistent with prior checkers; Ofcom's 31 Jul 2025 probe covered 34 sites run by Kick, 8579 LLC, AVS Group and Trendio.

eSafety's FAQ ('lists reflect eSafety's views as at 10 December 2025') names Discord, GitHub, Google Classroom, LEGO Play, Messenger, Pinterest, Roblox, Steam and Steam Chat, WhatsApp and YouTube Kids as not age-restricted, and Facebook, Instagram, Kick, Reddit, Snapchat, Threads, TikTok, X, YouTube as age-restricted; the 5 Nov 2025 release named nine and Twitch's later addition did not appear in the extracts (prior knowledge: added Dec 2025). eSafety stresses the lists may change as services evolve, that the classification is ultimately a matter for a court unless the Government prescribes platforms, and that Discord, Roblox and Steam had to submit self-assessments. Not searched: whether the list changed after Dec 2025.

Date (14 Jul 2025), prototype age-verification app, and 'self-declaration insufficient' confirmed (CMS; Digital Poland; Inside Privacy). Corrections: the guidelines apply to platforms accessible to minors EXCEPT micro and small enterprises, and are non-binding (Commission will use them as a 'significant and meaningful' benchmark). Verification is expected for adult content and high-risk environments; estimation is recommended only where verification is disproportionate. The app is a pilot/stopgap until the EU Digital Identity Wallet (expected end-2026); risk reviews must be repeated at least annually.

Discord disclosed 3 Oct 2025 that a third-party support provider's ticketing system was compromised, ~70,000 users' government-ID photos (age-appeal reviews) may have been exposed, and attackers' larger claims (variously 2.1m IDs, 1.6 TB, 5.5m users) were called inaccurate extortion. Contested details: vendor named as 5CA in some reports and as a Zendesk instance in others; timing reported as 20 Sep in one account and 22-24 Sep in another; alleged vishing of a support agent is single-source. Also exposed: names, emails, last-4 card digits, IPs, support transcripts; ransom demand reportedly $5m then $3.5m, refused.

AP (7 Aug 2025) confirms Sentinel is being open-sourced and led to ~1,200 NCMEC reports in H1 2025; trade press adds it scans ~6bn chat messages/day in one-minute snapshots and has run since late 2024. The '35% proactive' share did not appear in the search extracts (prior checkers attribute it to Roblox's newsroom post). The 24,522 / 20.3m 2024 figures were not searched (budget); prior checkers note NCMEC's 2024 total is usually ~20.5m.

March 2026 announcement confirmed: Horizon Worlds and Events delisted from the Quest Store 31 Mar 2026, app removed from Quest and VR building/publishing ended after 15 Jun 2026, continuing only in the Meta Horizon mobile app; Meta cited >4x mobile MAU growth in 2025. Whether removal happened as scheduled was not confirmable (all results pre-date 15 Jun). The Feb 2022 Personal Boundary half was not searched (budget); prior checkers agree it became user-adjustable (off/2ft/4ft) in March 2022, so 'always-on' is only true of the launch.

Stoner Cats: $1m civil penalty, 13 Sep 2023, NFT destruction and Fair Fund — confirmed. Correction: Impact Theory (Aug 2023) resolved for approximately $6m in aggregate (disgorgement, interest and penalty; $500k was only the civil penalty), plus Fair Fund, token destruction and surrender of secondary royalties. Not searched (budget): Steam's 15 Oct 2021 blockchain ban and the SEC's 2025 'digital collectibles not securities' stance; prior checkers confirm both from memory.

Confirmed: final Article 50 guidelines issued 20 Jul 2026 (Stephenson Harwood), Code of Practice published June 2026 with 'about 190' signatories by end July 2026 (Commission digital-strategy page; MoFo 11 Sep 2026), obligations applying from 2 Aug 2026. Correction/nuance: under the Digital Omnibus on AI (political agreement May 2026; Council approval reported 29 Jun 2026, OJ publication not confirmed) the Art 50(2) machine-readable marking duty for generative systems already on the market before 2 Aug 2026 is deferred to 2 Dec 2026 — not Feb 2027 as the earlier checkers assumed. Guidelines accept plain-language notices, persistent badges or spoken statements but not a generic 'assistant' label or buried T&Cs; AI agents must say on whose behalf they act; content generated before 2 Aug 2026 need not be relabelled.

additional_findings: Method: WebFetch/curl were blocked, so every verdict rests on search-engine extracts of the cited pages, not full text; 12 of 12 searches used; claims 2 (AVS/£18m cap), 6 (24,522 reports), 7 (Personal Boundary) and 8 (Steam ban, SEC 2025 stance) were only partly searched and lean on prior-checker knowledge for the unsearched halves.

The Roblox state settlements have converged on a contractual template a successor world will be measured against: age assurance for all users, under-18 chat restricted by default to the same or adjacent age band, adult-to-under-16 contact only via verified trusted connections, safe-content mode by default for under-16s, with liquidated damages on breach (Kansas $10m; South Dakota up to $5.4m extra) and a most-favoured-nation clause for Alabama that propagates stricter terms across states.

Roblox now re-runs age checks when behavioural signals suggest a user is much older or younger than their band, and says bands may vary by region/product — age assurance is a continuous process, not a one-off gate.

Roblox's Q2 2026 10-Q (as of 30 Jul 2026) lists settled states as Alabama, Mississippi, Nevada, South Dakota and West Virginia and says it is negotiating with others; Kansas followed 29 Sep 2026. South Dakota's package is reported as $15m over four years ($8.6m guaranteed), so the brief's '$54m' total should be given as a range until Mississippi's amount is found.

Ofcom's age-assurance orders carry daily penalties (£1,000/day for 8579 LLC, £200-250/day for Kick) and a duty to disclose a full list of operated sites; the 31 Jul 2025 investigation covered 34 sites across four operators, so enforcement is portfolio-wide per operator rather than per site.

eSafety's not-restricted status is advisory: unless the Government prescribes platforms, whether a service is an 'age-restricted social media platform' is ultimately for a court, and Discord, Roblox and Steam had to file written self-assessments with evidence — a successor world should keep a documented primary-purpose self-assessment ready.

The EU age-verification app is explicitly a stopgap until the EU Digital Identity Wallet (expected end-2026); the DSA minors guidelines also expect a documented risk review at least annually and on significant design changes, with features classified low/medium/high risk.

Discord breach: beyond ID photos, the vendor ticketing system exposed last-four card digits, IPs and full support transcripts, and the intrusion was reportedly social-engineered via a phone call to a support agent; vendor identity (5CA vs 'a Zendesk instance') and dates remain contested in press accounts.

Sentinel reportedly processes ~6 billion chat messages a day in one-minute snapshots and has run since late 2024; the '35% caught proactively' figure could not be found outside Roblox's own post, so treat it as company-reported.

Meta's Horizon Worlds exit ended VR world building/publishing on 15 Jun 2026 and was justified by >4x mobile MAU growth in 2025 amid ~10% Reality Labs layoffs; the social-VR market for a successor world is therefore smaller and less contested, but the harassment evidence base it generated remains the reference set regulators cite.

AI Act Art 50 guidelines (20 Jul 2026) set concrete disclosure forms for AI characters/NPCs: plain-language notice, persistent badge or spoken statement, never a generic 'assistant' label or T&C-only disclosure; autonomous agents must state on whose behalf they act; extra care is expected where children are in the audience; pre-2 Aug 2026 content needs no retro-labelling; marking duty for pre-existing generative systems deferred to 2 Dec 2026 under the Digital Omnibus.
